Pieces exist (ckpt needs a hook in transformer_obs_encoder.py; autocast absent; frozen:True crashes dp_policy.py:675-681; register drop needs aggregate_feature edit; Normalize must be mirrored in dp_policy.py:650-661; peft/bitsandbytes/torchao absent in both envs) but the deliverable needs them collapsed into one table the user can decide from, given the 'no code' framing.

Dataset and batch for the DINOv3 run are unspecified: the brief says ~75 episodes (dataset_depth.zarr.zip, 0901 set) and batch 64, but the E/A/C ablation and the deployment candidate A were trained on the 9_9_26 set (62 ep, 19,194 frames, 518 it/epoch) at batch 32; the obs statistics were measured on the 75-ep set. Wall-clock per epoch at the real 518 it/epoch × 200 was never derived for L/H+ (ViT-B anchor: ~97 s/epoch uncontended).

No baseline or success metric exists for judging a DINOv3 run: the A (ViT-CLIP) checkpoint was flown closed-loop on 2026-09-13 (46 engagements, new can) with no yaw/bearing analysis; no L/R-balanced underwater observe run with the NEW can exists; and the only discriminating tool (policy_yaw_vs_can.py) showed all encoders unresponsive in 3 of 4 runs with the old can. Without this, a DINOv3 result is indistinguishable from baseline and 'expected benefit vs the OOD failure' cannot be answered.

Zero evidence that RGB pretraining carries usable signal on THIS encoding ([inv_depth, validity, inv_depth], no mean/std): the plan's 'CLIP pretraining benefit nearly nil on depth' (DP_TRAJECTORY_PLAN.ko.md:154-156) was never tested (no pretrained-vs-scratch ablation on depth exists in the repo; DeFM's ViT numbers use per-image min-max + 3× replicate + ImageNet norm, a different encoding). If pretraining contributes nothing here, DINOv3's only advantage (LVD-1689M prior) is moot and the decision reduces to 'bigger ViT on 62 episodes' — which the 49× train/val gap of ViT-B argues against.

Seed variance is unknown: every ablation variant is a single seed (42); held-out pos RMSE differences between encoders are 17.7 vs 21.1 mm and underwater rankings rested on one run. A single DINOv3 run vs a single A run cannot separate encoder effect from seed noise; no repeat-seed spread for the held-out or yaw-vs-can metric has ever been measured.

No small-data fine-tuning recipe for a 300M+ DINOv3 encoder: the only UMI-setting size sweep (Data Scaling Laws) used ~1,824 demos at effective batch 256 on 8 GPUs; the project's obs_encoder_lr 3e-5 / wd 1e-6 / 200 epochs were tuned for ResNet34/ViT-B and ViT-B already overfits 49×. Layer-wise lr decay, partial freezing (first-N blocks), and the DINOv3-specific small-data papers (arXiv 2508.21041, MDPI Sensors 26:5285) are unverified; whether LoRA (peft) is even installable in umi2 was not checked.

Deploy-side total GPU budget is unquantified: station process 7.5 GB + FoundationStereo (46 ms, VRAM unmeasured here) + SAM2/FoundationPose + DINOv3 (L 0.6–1.8 GB, H+ 1.8–5.2 GB, 7B 13.5 GB resident) — and whether the policy worker shares the FS process/GPU. End-to-end predict() latency with 411 cond tokens at DDIM 8 (vs 403 today) was not measured; only the encoder forward (5–43 ms) was. The plan-age budget (obs age p50 0.5 s, 41 % late plans at DDIM 16) is the real constraint.

contradictions: Batch size: the orchestrator brief and BOTH GPU benchmarks assume batch 64 (128 images/step), but the prior-evidence reader shows every real run (09.07 deployed ckpt and E/A/C) overrode dataloader.batch_size=32 (.hydra/overrides.yaml). At 64 images/step the compute-recipes conclusion 'ViT-L full FT needs grad-checkpointing' is wrong for bf16 (bench2: 64 img 17.92 GiB fits without ckpt) and unmeasured for the fp32 loop actually used.

HF gating: the license-claim verifier asserts 'every DINOv3 weight on HF (facebook/* and timm/*) is gated — HF token + license acceptance required', whereas the gating-claim verifier and MEASURE's download_check.log/gate_check.log show timm/* repos gated=False, anonymous config.json download OK, and vit_large_patch16_dinov3.lvd1689m downloaded in 26 s. The measurement wins; the license verifier's operational caveat is false for the timm route.

Benchmark cross-contamination: MEASURE reports its first run was contaminated by foreign process PID 9708 'timeout 590 python dinov3_bench2.py' (11–17 GB) — i.e. the compute-recipes bench2 numbers were themselves taken while MEASURE's first sweep shared the GPU. This explains bench2's anomalous H+ rows (frozen fwd 703 ms vs MEASURE 328 ms; LoRA-like 2293 ms; autocast inference 9.05 vs 11.9 ms) — cite MEASURE's dinov3_bench.csv (0/62 rows flagged) as the artifact, not dinov3_bench2_result.json.

7B fine-tune feasibility: MEASURE's caveat says 'any real 7B fine-tune (even LoRA with fp32 master) is out of reach on one 32 GB card' (pure-bf16 full FT OOM at 32 img with ckpt), while compute-recipes' frozen-base + 0.33 M-param LoRA-stand-in with ckpt fits at 64 images (18.56 GiB) — and the verifier adds that the workspace's EMA deepcopy of the frozen 7B (+12.5 GiB) pushes 128 img to ~37.5 GiB. The two are different modes; the blanket MEASURE statement is too strong for a LoRA route at batch 32 without an encoder EMA copy, but real peft LoRA was never measured.

timm cfg fixed_input_size: dinov3-facts claim says False with min_input_size (3,128,128); the verifier and compute-recipes reader show timm 1.0.29 sets fixed_input_size=True and has no min_input_size (eva.py:1396). No practical effect (dynamic_img_size=True), but the claim text must not be cited.

7B ObjectNet: dinov3-facts claim cites 91.1 for 7B vs 78.6 H+ ('7B still clearly ahead'); the verifier finds 91.1 is the IN-R column / a model-card duplicate and the paper's own table gives 79.0 — a 0.4-pt gap, not 12.5. The 'largest buys global-task accuracy' narrative survives only on Oxford-H and NYU.

Project depth encoding as described by the depth-input researcher (claims 2–3 'why_it_matters': 'per-frame anchor-scaled linear depth, umi_aquatic_dataset.py:349-386, [0,10 m]→[0,1]', 'the weakest raw variant') contradicts the depth-obs code reader and the DeFM verifier: the obs is FIXED-range INVERSE depth 0.20–3.00 m from build_zarr.py:59-69, channels [inverse_depth, validity_mask, inverse_depth], dataset class umi_dataset.UmiDataset (task yaml :95), not umi_aquatic_dataset. Any inference drawn from 'linear normalised depth is fragile' (Vanishing Depth) is misapplied.

'No major RGB-D foundation model feeds depth to an unmodified RGB ViT' (depth-input claim 5) is rejected by its verifier: LanguageBind (ICLR 2024) feeds 3×-replicated depth into an OpenCLIP ViT-L and beats ImageBind on NYU-D; ImageBind's depth encoder is ViT-S-class (384-d), not ViT-B. The corrected reading weakens the 'modality mismatch' argument against simply swapping the backbone.

Data Scaling Laws recipe: policy-encoders claim states batch 32, ~800 demos, GroupNorm; the verifier shows effective batch 256 on 8 A800 (32/process), ~1,824 demos (50 % of 3,648), and GroupNorm is a no-op for the pretrained ViT. The 'closest analogue' is ~25× the project's demo count at 4× its effective batch.

'Current encoder' identity: the brief and research treat vit_base_patch16_clip_224.openai as the current encoder; the non-vit depth workspace yaml (train_diffusion_transformer_umi_depth_workspace.yaml:49-50) defaults to resnet34.a1_in1k with CLIP commented out, and the deployed default ckpt (POLICY_CKPT_DEFAULT, config/hw_mpc.yaml:470) is the 09.07 ResNet34 run; ViT-CLIP is a candidate flown once (0913). A DINOv3 comparison must state which baseline (ResNet34 deployed vs ViT-CLIP A) it is measured against.

Register/token handling: research (dinov3-facts, compute-recipes) frames the 4 register tokens as something the encoder 'must slice [5:]', while both code readers show feature_aggregation: null forwards all 201 tokens and the denoiser self-sizes (cond_pos_emb 1×411×768) with no code change; dropping registers is optional and itself requires an edit in aggregate_feature plus station pass-through. Not a blocker, contrary to the research framing.

Normalisation shift magnitude: the depth-obs reader states inputs sit '~2 std off' the pretraining distribution; the depth-input verifier shows the error is affine per pixel (ch0: +2.1 at x=0, −1.25 at x=1, range compressed ~4.4×), so only near-far/invalid pixels are ~2 std off. Same conclusion (matters only if frozen), different number — cite the affine form.
